commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

17	// SAME raw body as `map[string]any`, which the repository merges into the
18	// existing subdoc via `mongo.MergeDeepJSON` by KEY PRESENCE: a key absent
19	// in the body is left alone; an explicit `false`/`0`/`""`/`null` is
20	// applied and overrides the stored value (so `null` sent on a top-level
21	// nullable like `log_channel_id` clears it); nested objects recurse;
22	// slices replace wholesale; maps merge per-key.

25	// decoder (silently drops unknown keys, parity with Mongoose) — only

30	// NOT enforce zod's REQUIRED-ness inside a present nested object, so a

15	// (§8 del contrato original, §4 del contrato v4). Vertical NUEVA sin
16	// contraparte en el Node api-db, así que no hay un zod que mirrorear byte a
17	// byte — pero, a diferencia del resto del paquete
18	// (moderation_flow_runs_validations.go, etc.), esta vertical NUNCA responde
19	// 400 por `scope`, el descriptor de curva (`curve_mode`, `curve_multiplier`,
20	// `curve_thresholds`), `voice_metric`, un delta de XP, `limit` u `offset`
21	// ausentes o mal formados: el contrato v4 lo pide explícito para el
22	// descriptor completo ("ausentes o inválidos → formula, multiplicador 1,
23	// tabla vacía y métrica xp — nunca un error") y aquí se aplica el MISMO
24	// criterio a los demás, porque todos son parámetros de LECTURA/ESCRITURA
25	// DERIVADA (§3), no validaciones de negocio — el repositorio ya clampa
26	// limit/offset a sus rangos (ver LevelingRepository.Top). El único 400 real
27	// de esta vertical es `user_id` ausente dentro de una entrada de
28	// `POST /xp/bulk` (no tiene default razonable) o un body que ni siquiera es

32	// cascada (ver buildLevelingCurve): un `curve_thresholds` vacío o inválido
33	// NUNCA arrastra `curve_mode` de vuelta a "formula", ni viceversa — así una
34	// tabla manual a medio configurar (`curve_mode=manual&curve_thresholds=`,
35	// el caso de una tabla vacía) sigue siendo modo manual con cero umbrales,
36	// no degrada silenciosamente a la curva automática.

44	// tamaño habitual de un leaderboard "top". El repositorio clampa el valor
